workItem: dashboard: the collision oracle discards the most severe overlaps

originalIntentOfTheExclusion.removedComment: Nesting and full containment are how layered interfaces are built; only text intruding on unrelated text is a defect.
originalIntentOfTheExclusion.intent: Stop a wrapper being reported as colliding with its own contents. A parent box always encloses its children, so a naive all-pairs sweep makes every correct layout look catastrophically broken.
originalIntentOfTheExclusion.whyItWasTheWrongInstrument: The intent is about LINEAGE, and geometry was only ever a proxy for it. Lineage implies enclosure, but enclosure does not imply lineage. The proxy is therefore sound only for the ancestor/descendant case that the adjacent related() terms already decide exactly, and unsound for every cross-branch pair, which it silently discards.
originalIntentOfTheExclusion.twoGuardsNotOne: text_collisions already carried a second, correct guard: related(state, key, other) walks the parent chain. duplicates_semantic_ancestor separately handles the text-inheritance problem (a wrapper appearing to hold its child's string). Neither needed the geometric term.

ancestorVersusUnrelated.mustBeReported: enclosure between elements on different branches - a genuine collision, and the most severe one
ancestorVersusUnrelated.decidedBy: related() - DOM lineage, exact, no tolerance
ancestorVersusUnrelated.noLongerDecidedBy: contains() - box geometry, carried a +/-1.0px fudge

corroboratingArtifact.significance: The census that produced every overlap number in this workstream - including the 2298.5px2 that opened this item - excludes ancestor/descendant pairs by DOM lineage ALONE and carries no geometric containment rule, while using thresholds identical to the comparator (MIN_AREA 16, MIN_FRAC 0.08). The two geometric terms were the comparator's only predicate-level divergence from its own oracle, so this change is a reconciliation, not a new rule.

ancestorVersusUnrelated.changeShape: deletion, not a special case: the two contains() terms and the now-dead fn contains were removed; related() is untouched

blockedOnFixtureAuthor.statement: The oracle fix is correct and complete, but the qualification score fell 44/44 -> 42/44 because two frozen manifests encode the BLIND oracle's output. Both regressions are 'content mismatch' on finding COUNT and FIRST LINE, never a missed detection: both mutants still report status=Fail.
blockedOnFixtureAuthor.whyIDidNotFixIt: backtest/fixtures/**/expected.json is fixture-author's write set and is explicitly forbidden to me. I did not edit, suppress or work around it.
blockedOnFixtureAuthor.gateMechanism: backtest/src/fixture.rs:385 requires report.findings.len() == mutation.primary_findings exactly, and mutation.finding to equal the FIRST finding line. An additional overlap finding therefore breaks both conditions, and overlap lines sort ahead of the previously-first line in both cases.

contradictedClaim.claim: frozen-marker-left is still DETECTED, via the x-shift finding rather than the overlap finding, so the fixture qualifies today and will tighten automatically if the oracle is widened.
contradictedClaim.finding: The 'will tighten automatically' half is FALSE. backtest/fixtures/frozen-offset/expected.json freezes primaryFindings at 1 and pins finding to the x-shift line, so a widened oracle necessarily produces 2 findings and the fixture BREAKS rather than tightening. The dashboard assignment inherited this claim; it is the only part of the assignment that did not hold.
